A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed methods and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original MNIST experiments comparing AEP, EP and VF under symmetric initialization, fixed asymmetry and feedforward connectivity, with additional analyses in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains the MNIST experiments and adds original Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 evaluations, plus constrained-input stability experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The Asymmetric EP correction, Dyadic EP energy and dynamics, and parameter-update procedures remain unchanged. AEP is renamed AsymEP. The additional architectures and constrained-input experiments apply the existing algorithms under new experimental settings.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates handwritten-digit classification on MNIST only. V2 adds Fashion-MNIST apparel classification and CIFAR-10 natural-image classification in Sections 5.4–5.5, substantially broadening the represented data and domains.

E2.justification: V2 adds experimentally evaluated backpropagation comparisons: a Fashion-MNIST reference result in Table 1 and a direct CNN comparison in Table 2. V1 discusses backpropagation theoretically but evaluates only EP and VF against AEP. The new true-gradient reference substantially strengthens the comparator set.

E3.justification: Retained MNIST settings match. New protocols include matched-parameter comparisons across dynamics and connectivity, deeper Fashion-MNIST networks, a 40-epoch CIFAR-10 CNN evaluation, and output-variance measurement under constrained input projections. The stability experiment's budget is inconsistent: Table 3 lists 40 epochs, whereas Table 5 reports epoch 80.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of dynamics, connectivity and depth, plus an all-to-all MNIST stability control varying input-projection strength at fixed structural asymmetry. Appendix G.3 tests whether training suppresses oscillations independently of increasing input magnitude. These extend the retained asymmetry, learning-speed and Jacobian analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard deviations over ten runs for the retained MNIST experiments. V2 additionally specifies five seeds for CIFAR-10 and introduces a paired t-test comparing Dyadic EP with backpropagation, reporting p = 0.75. No increased run count is established for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The retained MNIST results match, including 92.7 ± 0.5% for AEP/AsymEP versus 64.3 ± 2.0% for VF in the feedforward experiment. V2 adds extensive results: Table 2 reports CIFAR-10 accuracies of 90.66 ± 0.25% for backpropagation, 90.69 ± 0.14% for Dyadic EP, 89.74 ± 0.14% for AsymEP and 10.00 ± 0.00% for VF. Fashion-MNIST and stability results are also newly reported.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives AsymEP as a first-order projection of Dyadic EP. Appendix G.3 adds spectral stability reasoning and derivatives for constrained input projections. The Dyadic gradient identity also changes from including an O(beta^3) remainder in v1 Eq. (69) to an exact expression justified by linearity in v2 Eq. (71).

C1.justification: The central claim of exact-gradient learning for arbitrary stationary non-conservative systems is retained. V2 characterizes Dyadic EP as an independent first-principles generalization of existing Dyadic Learning, and its conclusion expands the empirical claim from AEP on MNIST to both proposed algorithms across three datasets.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning expressivity benefits from asymmetric connectivity and stabilization through input-induced diagonal Jacobian contributions. Appendix G.3 explicitly leaves a complete stability analysis outside scope and discusses residual oscillations and time averaging. Earlier hardware-implementation and temporal-memory limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 retains the MNIST implementation information and substantially expands documentation through Tables 3–4 and Appendix G.6. Additions include CNN9 architecture, initialization, augmentation, optimizer and learning-rate schedule, weight averaging, target smoothing, and method-specific relaxation limits and stopping tolerances.

R1.justification: V1 relates Dyadic EP primarily to Dual Propagation as a symmetric special case. V2 substantially revises this positioning by acknowledging Dyadic Learning and describing an independent generalization to arbitrary force fields, adding related works by Høier and Zach, Høier et al., and Nest and Høier. It also adds Millidge et al. and Osat and Golestanian, while removing Galley et al. (2014).

P1.justification: V2 renames AEP to AsymEP, tightens several explanatory passages, rewrites and relocates Out-of-Equilibrium Mechanics from Appendix E to C, and reorganizes subsequent appendices. It also adds an Impact Statement. The overall main-text narrative and organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds benchmark Tables 1–2 and appendix Tables 4–6, and expands v1's hyperparameter Table 1 into v2 Table 3 with a stability-experiment column. All seven original figures are retained with updated method labels and some relocation. The substantial addition of result and configuration displays goes beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important validation gap: v1 tested only shallow MNIST networks and did not directly evaluate Dyadic EP. The Fashion-MNIST comparisons, CNN9 CIFAR-10 evaluation against backpropagation, and constrained-input stability control provide substantially broader evidence, supported by added derivations and implementation details. The 40-versus-80-epoch inconsistency in Tables 3 and 5 limits reproducibility of the stability experiment, but does not outweigh these substantial gains.
